chapter: Mexico trip and Charlie Tolles band
title: Joe Oliver and the early Kid band
summary: He knew Joe Oliver, older by five or six years, who came up in a youngsters' brass band and later led his own; he recalls Oliver's wife Stella and Armstrong leaving with him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Ask him did he know Joe Oliver?

Did you know Joe Oliver? Oh yeah, Joe. He was on the corner from Joe Oliver. That's the time I used to go to the Royal Guard. He got that job out today. Bless you know. Yeah, he was the king out there. And then when he was older than me, he was about five or six years old than me. But I know them when they first had a band organized. There was a brother named Kintin. He had all these youngsters from fifteen to eighteen years old playing a bass band. He used to carry them all around in different places up and down the country. Then when they come back there, Joe got good. Then Joe, she just made up a band himself. And everybody played with him. The first lick I hit on the guitar was Joe, Joe, Oliver and old man Umphrey. He stayed in California a long time too. The Clown-Eyed player. The Clown-Eyed player. Yeah, Clown-Eyed player. And we was passing there by the plate. I couldn't go in the ball. It was a body there. If they happened to slip me in. And they say, you reckon you can play a piece in it? I said, I tried to play something new. I said, play the blues. They played the blues. I played. And that sucked me playing with a band after that, you know.
Who was in that band? Kinkins Band or Jenkins?
Who was in that band? Jenkins. Jenkins. Jenkins.
He was talking about the Kid Band with Joe Oliver.
Joe Oliver. Oh. Joe Oliver, oh. The only one I can know is uh, uh, uh, that's part of the name Rob Palmer. Mm-hmm. Cimbone player. Is he up there yet?

Oh, Chicago. They had him, Hellman Umphrey on the, on the Clown-Eyed. He said, he had a bass. And he said, it was old time fellas. I can't remember them, you know, when he first started out. And then when he left here, he left here with a bunch of fellas from here, you know. Then he sent to Lewis Armstrong. And I said, they stayed together. But he was still living around the corner from here. On the street. And then when his wife come back, after she died, she come right back there, and they're there about six months. And then she moved, you know.
Well, she's on Phillip Street now. On Phillip Street?
Yeah. Stella Oliver is on Phillip Street now. Oh, yeah. She lives right near John Casimir. Oh, yeah. I see her once in a while. Yeah.
